Lightfield [...] That created friction.

I didn’t want to be the person saying, “Just tell me what needs doing.” I wanted to already know and take more of that mental load on myself. So I built Daddy Issues.

It gives dads a weekly family briefing that connects things like your kids, calendar, responsibilities and previous tasks to surface what you might otherwise only realize later.

It’s not about being perfectly organized. It’s about anticipating a little earlier, taking more ownership, and hopefully avoiding some unnecessary arguments along the way.

It’s completely free for now, and I’m genuinely curious whether this is useful to other dads too. I’d love to hear what it gets right, what it misses, or what you’d change. ❤️

Hey Dads 👋

I built Daddy Issues because I kept noticing the same thing in our family:

My wife somehow seemed to know what was coming up. What the kids would need. What we should start thinking about now so it wouldn’t become stressful later.

I wanted to do that too.

I’m an involved dad, but I found thinking ahead surprisingly hard. I’d remember the obvious things, but miss the small connections around them and end up reacting once something was already on the table.

That created friction.
